description.narrative: The Project will provide financial and technical support to the National Disaster Risk Management Fund (NDRMF), which is being established as a government-owned non-bank financial intermediary with a corporate structure. The NDRMF will reduce the socio-economic and fiscal vulnerability of the country and its population to natural hazards by prioritizing and financing investments in disaster risk reduction and preparedness that have high economic benefits, taking into account climate change, as well as disaster risks and their impacts. The government will pass on ADB loan funds to the NDRMF as a grant, for on-granting by NDRMF to eligible implementing partners. The NDRMF will finance up to 70% of the cost of eligible subprojects that will enhance Pakistan's resilience to extreme weather events and other natural hazards. The NDRMF will also enter into insurance arrangements to develop markets for the transfer of residual risks that cannot be mitigated.

description.narrative: Increased and sustainable institutional and physical capacity to reduce the socio-economic and fiscal impacts of natural disasters and climate change.

At least 3 million people who are highly vulnerable to the negative impacts of multiple natural hazards as of 2016 are safe and have become more resilient against the direct and indirect impacts of multiple natural hazards by 2024. (2016 Baseline: n/a). Progress/Status: To be assessed during Project completion review. Data Source: Independent evaluation reports financed by the NDRMF and/or the government; damage and loss reports provided by the National Disaster Management Authority; and reports by development partners and third-party entities Base year: 2016 Baseline value: N
Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: An additional 50 public buildings financed by the NDRMF (in the social sector) are made safe and resistant to multiple hazards by Q4 2022. (2016 baseline: 0). Achievement: 44 Progress/Status: 88% of the target achieved. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF.

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: At least 125 km of new or retrofitted flood protection infrastructure financed by the NDRMF are constructed by Q1 2024 (2016 baseline: 0 km). Achievement: 114.19 Progress/Status: 91% of the target achieved. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF.

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: CBDRM plans completed in 73 vulnerable union councils or urban centers by Q4 2022 (2016 Baseline = 0) Achievement: 76 Progress/Status: Around 450 community based disaster management committees were formed across Pakistan whereby providing general as well as specialized trainings to approximately 8,000 volunteers for enhancing their capabilities to act as first responders in case of disasters and emergencies. Data Source: Independent monitoring and NDRMF quarterly operations progress reports

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: The geographic coverage area of early warning systems increases by 10% by Q4 2021 (2016 baseline: 80%) Progress/Status: The target has been dropped through a memo for change in scope. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF. Actual value:

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: By Q2 2022, at least, 500 health care workers (including all qualified female workers) trained on different aspects of safety including IPC, good laboratory practices, and drugs testing. (2021 Baseline: 0) Achievement: 754 Progress/Status: Overachieved. of the 754 health care workers trained, 378 were females and 376 were males. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF.

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: By Q4 2023, the existing capacity of NIH and Provincial Public Health Laboratories in COVID-19 detection enhanced to 40,000 tests/month (2021 Baseline: 18,000 test/months. Achievement: 40,000 Progress/Status: Twelve (12) new and latest PCR machines along with associated hardware and software were delivered to NIH (on December 27, 2021) enhancing the capacity for conducting tests to more than 40,000 tests per month. 1 PCR Machine (Tianlong Gentier 96E can process up to 96 samples in 7 seconds in addition to sample preparation time. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF. Actual value: 40,000

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: By Q3 2021, at least 15 hospital, diagnostic laboratories, entry points, and isolation centers strengthened for COVID-19 preparedness and response. (2020 Baseline: 5) Achievement: More than 15 Progress/Status: Overachieved. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF. Actual value: More than 15

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: By Q2 2022, storage capacity of testing kits and equipment increased to 1 million testing kits per month. (2021 Baseline: 0.6 million kits/month) Achievement: 1000000 Progress/Status: Achieved.
Four (4) new cold rooms (each having capacity of 6-8 Tonnes) were delivered to NIH (on November 9, 2021) enhancing the storage capacity of testing kits up to 1 million. Data Source: Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF.

Output: Analytical work and products to improve fiscal management of disaster risks. Indicator: By Q4 2022, a gender-sensitive national DRF strategy is developed (2016 Baseline: None) Progress/Status: DRF Strategy is approved by the Board. Data Source: Approved DRF strategy, Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly progress reports of the NDRMF Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y

Progress/Status: Dropped by a change in scope memo. Data Source: Approved DRF strategy, Independent monitoring by ADB financed TA consultants and quarterly progress reports of the NDRMF Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y

Data Source: National emergency response plan. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2021 Target value: Y

Output: Increased investment to reduce vulnerability to disasters. Indicator: National level MHVRA (including climate change and gender related vulnerabilities) completed and 20 sub-national level MHVRAs completed by Q3 2019. Progress/Status: The target has been dropped through a memo for change in scope of DFAT grant and the grant proceeds have been reallocated for supporting COVID-19 preparedness and response. Data Source: Independent monitoring and quarterly operations progress reports of the NDRMF. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2020 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: A comprehensive ERP for the fund is developed and deployed by Q4 2022 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: First part of ERP i.e. standard business modules is up and running since Sep 2020. However, second part i.e. Grant Appraisal and Administration system was developed but could not be finalized during implementation period. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports of the fund. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: Communication, disclosure, and public relations strategies of the NDRMF are developed by March 2019 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: TA Consultant in consultation with relevant NDRMF staff has developed gender responsive communication strategy which has been approved by the management. Data Source: Fund progress reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: Fund implementation partner accreditation and subproject selection criteria are finalized and approved by the NDRMF by February 2019 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: Activity completed on time. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports of the fund. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: Income from the endowment fund finances 100% of NDRMF operating expenses by Q1 2022 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: Operating cost is covered from the endowment fund since January 2022. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports of the fund. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2022 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: Requisite governance, operational, fiduciary, and safeguard (including gender) procedures, polices, and systems are in place by February 2019 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: The Fund's BoD has approved a number of manuals, policies, procedures and systems that were developed and finalized through a collaborative effort of the TA consultants and the relevant staff of the Fund. These include: (i) procurement manual, (ii) financial management manual, (iii) human resource manual, (iv) investment guidelines, (v) environmental and social monitoring system (ESMS), (vi) limit of authority manual, (vii) organizational anti-sexual harassment policy, (viii) gender and development policy, (ix) diversity, equal opportunity and affirmative action policy, (x) code of conduct (xi) anti-corruption policy, (xii) grievance redressal and disciplinary policy, and (xiii) conflict of interest and disclosure policy.
Data Source: Donor review and NDRMF progress reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: The NDRMF is fully staffed (at least 20% of these staff members are women) and has a fully established office by March 2019 (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: With respect to staffing, a few senior management positions are lying vacant since long. Three senior positions of General Managers are vacant since the EA stopped appointments against these vacant senior positions considering the decreasing size of NDRMF's portfolio. Data Source: Minutes of the Board meeting and Fund periodic progress reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: The annual operational plan is prepared and approved every year within Q1. (2016 Baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Complied. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports of the fund. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: The endowment fund is invested in appropriate vehicles by June 2018 (2016 Baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Endowment fund is being invested in T-Bills for annual term Data Source: Fund progress reports Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2018 Target value: Y

Output: NDRMF established and made operational Indicator: The first batch of grant proposal approval by September 2019, (2016 Baseline: 0). Progress/Status: The first batch was approved in March 2019, the second in September 2019 and the third is Q1 2020. However, third batch subprojects could not be awarded because of diverting DRR funds ($30 million) for COVID-19 support. NDRMF has approved twenty-six (26) project proposals (i.e. 5 Non-Public & 21 Public sector) amounting US $ 120.56 Million.
The NDRMF performed well in awarding grants amounting to $25.3 million against $26 million repurposed for rehabilitation of disaster risk reduction (DRR) infrastructure damaged during 2022 floods. However, significant delays occurred in commencement of civil works due to late approval of initial environmental examination (IEE) reports on account of poor-quality submissions by FIPs and inadequate review at NDRMF because of overburdened staff. The contractors showed impressive performance initially, but lately slowed down the work because of disbursement issue. Data Source: Quarterly progress reports of the fund. Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2016 Baseline value: N Target year: 2019 Target value: Y
